title: Keep a loan's due dates on the day its contract names

blocks.text: A lender's support desk gets the same complaint every spring. A customer whose loan contract says "due on the 30th" is asked to pay on the 28th in March, April and every month after. Another, whose first instalment was due on 30 June and whose contract says "the last day of each month", is asked for 30 July instead of 31 July. Late fees are charged against both schedules.

The contract, as the lawyers wrote it: instalments are due on the same day of the month as the first one; in a month that has no such day, on that month's last day. A loan whose first instalment fell on the last day of its month is due on the last day of every month.
`Instalments.schedule` already lists the due dates. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Instalments.java`:

items: `dueDate(first, n)`: the due date of instalment `n`, where instalment `0` is due on `first`;
`isMonthEnd(date)`: whether a date is the last day of its month.

blocks.text: About four lines in total. The tests use loans that start in 2027 and 2028, leap years included.

cases.says: a year of instalments starts on the first due date and has one due date in each month, in order
a loan due on the 10th is due on the 10th of every month, whatever the months' lengths
a loan due on the 30th is due on 28 February and back on the 30th from March on
in a month without the contract's day, the instalment is due on that month's last day, without an error
a loan whose first instalment is due on 30 June, or on 29 February, is then due on the last day of every month
the 30th of a 30-day month counts as the last day of its month
28 February is the last day of its month in a common year and not in a leap year

origin.section: The Last Day of a Month Comes From an Adjuster, Not a Day Number

concepts: The last day of a month comes from TemporalAdjusters.lastDayOfMonth() or the month's length, not from a fixed day number; whether a date is a month end depends on its month and year.
plusMonths clamps the day to a shorter month's last day and forgets the original day, so chained month steps drift and don't reverse; each date of a series is computed from the first one.
